theme: Keeping data on disk: persistence, the temporary directory and atomic writes

terms.definition: The ability of data to stay after the app closes, so it is still there next time.
terms.example: Persistence keeps the draft after the app closes.

terms.definition: A folder for short-lived files that the system may delete when it needs space.
terms.example: The cache file lives in the temporary directory.
terms.code:
import Foundation
let dir = URL.temporaryDirectory
let u = dir.appending(path: "cache.tmp")
print(u.lastPathComponent)
print(dir.hasDirectoryPath)

terms.definition: A save that writes to a temporary file first, so a crash cannot leave a half-written file.
terms.example: Use an atomic write for the settings file.

video.description:
Learn to explain saving files so they survive: Persistence, Temporary Directory & Atomic Write, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Persistence - The ability of data to stay after the app closes, so it is still there next time.
Temporary Directory - A folder for short-lived files that the system may delete when it needs space.
Atomic Write - A save that writes to a temporary file first, so a crash cannot leave a half-written file.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

한국어: Persistence: 앱이 종료된 뒤에도 데이터가 남아 다음에 다시 쓸 수 있는 성질

한국어: Atomic Write: 임시 파일에 먼저 써서 충돌이 나도 반쯤 쓰인 파일이 남지 않게 하는 저장 방식

landscape.hook: Can you explain Persistence, Temporary Directory and Atomic Write in English?

dialogue.title: The vanishing draft

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, the user's draft disappears when the app closes.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You need persistence. It keeps data after the app closes, so it is still there next time.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: But I saved the draft in the temporary directory, like `dir` in our code.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That is the problem. The temporary directory is for short-lived files, and the system can delete them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So where do I put the draft?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: In the documents folder of the app. That is real persistence for user files.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What if the app crashes while saving?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use an atomic write. It writes to a temporary file first, so a crash cannot leave half a file.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Is that the `.atomic` option in our code?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. An atomic write is safer for important data.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the temporary directory is only for short-lived data?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. Use persistence and an atomic write for what matters.
Persistence keeps the draft after the app closes.
